              example: Franklin, George
              readOnly: true

              title: Salutation

              type: string
              example: DR Franklin
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials

                dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: G.F.
              readOnly: true
            telephoneDisplay:
              title: Telephone display
              description: The stored E.164 telephone formatted for humans, derived at read time as
                the country code, a space, then the national digits grouped in threes from the left.
                The raw 'telephone' field stays in E.164 form.
              type: string
              example: '+61 412 345 678'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: The owner's customer code, formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where LAST3 is the
                upper-cased first three letters of lastName and NNNN is a global 4-digit zero-padded
                sequence equal to one more than the number of owners at the time this owner was created.
              type: string
              example: SMI-0007
              readOnly: true

              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              maximum: 9
              example: 4
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:

                the last two digits of the registrationDate year.

              readOnly: true

## Summary

I converted owner deletion to a soft-delete. Changes:

**Domain model** — `Owner.java`: added a `deleted` column (primitive `boolean`, defaulting to `false` so a newly created owner is never null/true), with `isDeleted()`/`setDeleted()`.

The DELETE endpoint still responds 204 (2xx) via the existing `RespondWithNoContent` step, and `GET /api/owners/{id}` continues to load and return the row afterward with `deleted: true`.

**Create-time duplicate/identity checks** — both now skip flagged owners:
- `RejectDuplicateIdentity.java` — the 409-blocking identity + household-duplicate scan `continue`s past deleted owners, so a normally-blocking duplicate is allowed when the only match is soft-deleted.
- `AssignPossibleDuplicate.java` — the soft-match flag likewise ignores deleted owners.

**API contract** — `openapi.yml`: added a read-only `deleted` boolean to the `Owner` schema (not `OwnerFields`, so it's output-only). The generated `OwnerDto` gets the field and MapStruct maps `owner.deleted → dto.deleted` by name, so it surfaces in GET responses.

**Schema** — added the `deleted` column (`BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL`, `BIT(1)` for MySQL) to all four DB schemas (hsqldb used by the tests, plus h2/postgres/mysql for consistency). Existing seed inserts list columns explicitly, so the default applies cleanly.
